bull_bear.body:
- Plant located adjacent to the HPCL Visakha Refinery, which supplies the major raw material Propylene and is stated to be able to meet the Company's full Propylene requirement, so there are no stated constraints on production capability
- Two alternative Propylene sources developed (BPCL and GAIL) for emergency need, though the Company states these are not economical due to high logistic costs
- Sales realisation supported by Anti-Dumping Duties imposed by the Govt. of India on imports of the product from certain countries
- Sustained safety record — 21.29 million accident-free man-hours over the last 17 years, National Safety Award 2025 (Prashansa Patra, 4th level) and FICCI Excellence in Safety 2025 award
- Associate of The Andhra Sugars Ltd., with The Andhra Sugars Limited and Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Limited as promoters
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-source raw-material dependence on Propylene from the HPCL refinery — MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' states the Company depends on its major raw material Propylene from a single source, the HPCL refinery. Two alternative sources, BPCL and GAIL, have been developed only for emergency need and the Company itself states sourcing from them is not economical due to high logistic costs, so the mitigation is not commercially usable in normal operation.
- Product-price exposure to global petrochemical oversupply, particularly new Chinese capacity — Management attributes the decline in its own profitability to the additional petrochemical capacities built up in China, which caused prices of most petrochemicals to decline in Asia and put substantial margin pressure in India. Performance is stated to depend to a large extent on international supply, demand and prices for the Company's products.
- Import competition and dumping not covered by Anti-Dumping Duty — While Anti-Dumping Duties on imports from certain countries are expected to support realisations, management flags dumping of the products from sources other than those covered by the Duty, and cheaper imports, as drivers of overall performance.
- New domestic competition from BPCL and IOCL Oxo-Alcohols plants — MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' flags BPCL & IOCL Oxo Alcohols competitive prices as a factor that may impact the Company's performance, even as it argues a demand-supply gap persists after those plants come on line.
- Crude price and exchange-rate volatility — MD&A states crude prices and exchange-rate fluctuations are a matter of concern, and that product prices are influenced by crude prices and exchange fluctuations; currency fluctuations are separately listed among threats.
- Unexecuted land lease for the site on which the plant stands — The 30-year lease of 75 acres from Visakhapatnam Port Trust, on which the Oxo-Alcohol Plant is established, expired on 26.6.2019 and renewal remains unresolved through a Writ Petition, a High Court order directing execution of the Lease Deed, a VPT appeal (WA No. 688 of 2022) and a judgement on 3.11.2025; the Lease Deed is still unexecuted and lease accounting under Ind AS 116 is provisional on the Company's own bid amount. Security of tenure over the plant site is therefore unsettled.
- Regulatory power-cost liabilities (FPPCA) under appeal — APERC, Kurnool levied Fuel & Power Purchase Cost Adjustment charges for FY2022-23 and FY2023-24, recovered in monthly instalments with regular power charges; the Company has appealed to APTEL, New Delhi, and the Board has made provisions pending disposal, which were recognised as exceptional items.
- Geopolitical disruption to the business environment — Management describes the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, Israel-Hamas war, the recently started Iran-Israel war, additional US tariffs and the resulting global slowdown as a big challenge that may impact performance; this sits in both Industry Structure and Future Outlook.

- Two alternative Propylene sources developed (BPCL and GAIL) for emergency need, though the Company states these are not economical due to high logistic costs
- Sales realisation supported by Anti-Dumping Duties imposed by the Govt. of India on imports of the product from certain countries
- Sustained safety record — 21.29 million accident-free man-hours over the last 17 years, National Safety Award 2025 (Prashansa Patra, 4th level) and FICCI Excellence in Safety 2025 award
- Associate of The Andhra Sugars Ltd., with The Andhra Sugars Limited and Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Limited as promoters
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Serve the domestic Oxo-Alcohols demand-supply gap from the existing 80,000 MTPA capacity, which management says is unconstrained on production capability because HPCL can meet the full Propylene requirement
- Dilute single-source raw-material risk by maintaining two developed alternative Propylene sources (BPCL and GAIL) for emergency need, while acknowledging they are uneconomical on logistics cost
- Pursue a cheaper fuel route via a Natural Gas supply — a NG term sheet was signed with GAIL in 2019, but the GAIL/APGDCL pipeline project has been cancelled and the Company is awaiting fresh tenders for a Kakinada to Visakhapatnam / Srikakulam pipeline
- Sustainability positioned as core to business development, focused on Decarbonization & Air Emission Control, Water & Biodiversity Conservation, Health & Safety and Community Development, with energy audits and renewable energy used to reduce GHG emissions
- Maintain safety as a top priority through continuous personnel training and strict regulatory compliance, sustaining an accident-free record
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capacity-addition, expansion or new-project programme. The Company operates a single Oxo-Alcohol plant of 80,000 MTPA existing capacity on 75 acres leased from Visakhapatnam Port Trust at Visakhapatnam, and management states there are no constraints on its production capability because HPCL is able to meet the full Propylene requirement. The only named project in the report is a fuel-supply initiative rather than a capacity project: the Natural Gas term sheet signed with GAIL in 2019, where the GAIL/APGDCL natural-gas pipe-laying work was held up and the project has finally been cancelled; fresh tenders have been called for laying a natural gas pipeline from Kakinada to Visakhapatnam / Srikakulam. No commissioning, ramp-up or debottlenecking timeline is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Estimated domestic Oxo-Alcohols demand of 4,00,000 MTPA growing at 8% to 10% per annum against the Company's existing 80,000 MTPA capacity leaves a demand-supply gap even after BPCL and IOCL plants come on line
- Sales realisation is expected to improve on account of Anti-Dumping Duties imposed by the Govt. of India on imports from certain countries and a forecast of reasonably better Indian GDP growth
- Additional petrochemical capacity built up in China drove Asian petrochemical price declines and put margin pressure on India, which management cites as the reason profitability declined this year
- Performance depends to a large extent on international supply and demand for the Company's products and their prices, influenced by crude prices, exchange fluctuations and dumping from sources not covered by Anti-Dumping Duty
- Ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, Israel-Hamas war, the recently started Iran-Israel war, US tariffs and geopolitical tensions have slowed the global economy and are described as a big challenge that may impact performance
- Competitive pricing from BPCL and IOCL Oxo-Alcohols plants, product dumping and currency fluctuations may impact performance to some extent

open.item: Management expects Company performance to be reasonably good in view of the forecast of better GDP growth for India, subject to the disrupted business environment from the wars, US trade war and geopolitical tensions.
Management flags dependence on Propylene from a single source, the HPCL refinery, with BPCL and GAIL developed only as emergency alternatives that are uneconomical on logistics cost.
Management flags that BPCL & IOCL Oxo-Alcohols competitive prices, dumping of the products and currency fluctuations may impact performance.

The lease of the 75 acres of Visakhapatnam Port Trust land on which the plant stands remains unexecuted following the High Court judgement of 3.11.2025, with Ind AS 116 lease accounting provisional on the Company's bid amount until the Lease Deed is executed.

The Company is awaiting fresh tenders for a Natural Gas pipeline from Kakinada to Visakhapatnam / Srikakulam after the GAIL/APGDCL pipe-laying project against its 2019 NG term sheet with GAIL was cancelled.
Management cites estimated domestic Oxo-Alcohols demand of 4,00,000 MTPA growing 8% to 10% per annum as the opportunity for its existing 80,000 MTPA capacity.
Management flags continued dependence on Propylene from the single HPCL refinery source, with BPCL and GAIL alternatives uneconomical on logistics cost.

The GAIL/APGDCL natural-gas pipeline project against the Company's 2019 NG term sheet has been cancelled, and fresh tenders have been called for a Kakinada to Visakhapatnam / Srikakulam pipeline on which the Company's natural-gas supply depends.

Two alternative sources, BPCL and GAIL, have been developed only for emergency need and the Company itself states sourcing from them is not economical due to high logistic costs, so the mitigation is not commercially usable in normal operation.

risks.risk: Product-price exposure to global petrochemical oversupply, particularly new Chinese capacity
risks.note: Management attributes the decline in its own profitability to the additional petrochemical capacities built up in China, which caused prices of most petrochemicals to decline in Asia and put substantial margin pressure in India. Performance is stated to depend to a large extent on international supply, demand and prices for the Company's products.

risks.risk: Import competition and dumping not covered by Anti-Dumping Duty
risks.note: While Anti-Dumping Duties on imports from certain countries are expected to support realisations, management flags dumping of the products from sources other than those covered by the Duty, and cheaper imports, as drivers of overall performance.

risks.risk: New domestic competition from BPCL and IOCL Oxo-Alcohols plants
risks.note: MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' flags BPCL & IOCL Oxo Alcohols competitive prices as a factor that may impact the Company's performance, even as it argues a demand-supply gap persists after those plants come on line.

MD&A states crude prices and exchange-rate fluctuations are a matter of concern, and that product prices are influenced by crude prices and exchange fluctuations; currency fluctuations are separately listed among threats.

risks.risk: Unexecuted land lease for the site on which the plant stands
risks.note: The 30-year lease of 75 acres from Visakhapatnam Port Trust, on which the Oxo-Alcohol Plant is established, expired on 26.6.2019 and renewal remains unresolved through a Writ Petition, a High Court order directing execution of the Lease Deed, a VPT appeal (WA No. 688 of 2022) and a judgement on 3.11.2025; the Lease Deed is still unexecuted and lease accounting under Ind AS 116 is provisional on the Company's own bid amount. Security of tenure over the plant site is therefore unsettled.

APERC, Kurnool levied Fuel & Power Purchase Cost Adjustment charges for FY2022-23 and FY2023-24, recovered in monthly instalments with regular power charges; the Company has appealed to APTEL, New Delhi, and the Board has made provisions pending disposal, which were recognised as exceptional items.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to the business environment
risks.note: Management describes the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, Israel-Hamas war, the recently started Iran-Israel war, additional US tariffs and the resulting global slowdown as a big challenge that may impact performance; this sits in both Industry Structure and Future Outlook.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: The Andhra Petrochemicals Limited is an Indian Oxo-Alcohols producer with an existing capacity of 80,000 MTPA at Visakhapatnam, operating as an Associate of The Andhra Sugars Ltd.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures Oxo-Alcohols, comprising 2 Ethyl Hexanol, Normal Butanol and Iso Butanol, from a single plant established on land leased from Visakhapatnam Port Trust adjacent to the HPCL Visakha Refinery, which supplies its major raw material Propylene. It is an Associate of The Andhra Sugars Ltd. and has its Registered Office at Venkatarayapuram, Tanuku, Andhra Pradesh. Its equity shares are listed on BSE Limited, Mumbai, and the Company employed 275 people as on 31.3.2026.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- The Andhra Sugars Limited — related party: Promoter / parent; the Company is stated in the Corporate Overview to be an Associate of The Andhra Sugars Ltd. Counterparty for purchase of goods and services received; the AGM is held at the ASL Meeting Hall on The Andhra Sugars Ltd. premises at Venkatarayapuram, Tanuku.
- Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Limited — related party: Promoter; nominates two Directors (Sri V Raghunath and Sri K S S Aditya) to the Board.
- JOCIL Limited — related party: A subsidiary company of The Andhra Sugars Limited, the Promoter — i.e. a fellow group company, not a subsidiary of the Company. Listed in the RPT note with nil transactions and nil balances.
- Sri Mullapudi Venkatarayudu Memorial Medical Trust, Tanuku — related party: Entity under same management; CSR implementation counterparty.
- Sree Mullapudi Venkataramanamma Memorial Hospital, Venkatrayapuram — related party: Entity under same management; CSR implementation counterparty.
- Mullapudi Kamaladevi Cardio Vascular Centre, Tanuku — related party: Entity under same management.
- Sree Mullapudi Venkatarayudu Memorial Educational Trust, Tanuku — related party: Entity under same management.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Oxo-Alcohols:** 2 Ethyl Hexanol, Normal Butanol (N-Butanol), Iso Butanol (I-Butanol)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India — domestic Oxo-Alcohols demand, estimated by the Company at 4,00,000 MTPA growing 8% to 10% per annum
- Competes against imports; Anti-Dumping Duties imposed by Govt. of India on imports from certain countries

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- ISO 9001:2014
- ISO 45001:2018
- Bureau of Indian Standard Certification for all its products

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Estimated domestic Oxo-Alcohols demand of 4,00,000 MTPA growing at 8% to 10% per annum against the Company's existing 80,000 MTPA capacity leaves a demand-supply gap even after BPCL and IOCL plants come on line
- Sales realisation is expected to improve on account of Anti-Dumping Duties imposed by the Govt. of India on imports from certain countries and a forecast of reasonably better Indian GDP growth
- Additional petrochemical capacity built up in China drove Asian petrochemical price declines and put margin pressure on India, which management cites as the reason profitability declined this year
- Performance depends to a large extent on international supply and demand for the Company's products and their prices, influenced by crude prices, exchange fluctuations and dumping from sources not covered by Anti-Dumping Duty
- Ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, Israel-Hamas war, the recently started Iran-Israel war, US tariffs and geopolitical tensions have slowed the global economy and are described as a big challenge that may impact performance
- Competitive pricing from BPCL and IOCL Oxo-Alcohols plants, product dumping and currency fluctuations may impact performance to some extent

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Serve the domestic Oxo-Alcohols demand-supply gap from the existing 80,000 MTPA capacity, which management says is unconstrained on production capability because HPCL can meet the full Propylene requirement
- Dilute single-source raw-material risk by maintaining two developed alternative Propylene sources (BPCL and GAIL) for emergency need, while acknowledging they are uneconomical on logistics cost
- Pursue a cheaper fuel route via a Natural Gas supply — a NG term sheet was signed with GAIL in 2019, but the GAIL/APGDCL pipeline project has been cancelled and the Company is awaiting fresh tenders for a Kakinada to Visakhapatnam / Srikakulam pipeline
- Sustainability positioned as core to business development, focused on Decarbonization & Air Emission Control, Water & Biodiversity Conservation, Health & Safety and Community Development, with energy audits and renewable energy used to reduce GHG emissions
- Maintain safety as a top priority through continuous personnel training and strict regulatory compliance, sustaining an accident-free record

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no capacity-addition, expansion or new-project programme. The Company operates a single Oxo-Alcohol plant of 80,000 MTPA existing capacity on 75 acres leased from Visakhapatnam Port Trust at Visakhapatnam, and management states there are no constraints on its production capability because HPCL is able to meet the full Propylene requirement. The only named project in the report is a fuel-supply initiative rather than a capacity project: the Natural Gas term sheet signed with GAIL in 2019, where the GAIL/APGDCL natural-gas pipe-laying work was held up and the project has finally been cancelled; fresh tenders have been called for laying a natural gas pipeline from Kakinada to Visakhapatnam / Srikakulam. No commissioning, ramp-up or debottlenecking timeline is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Plant located adjacent to the HPCL Visakha Refinery, which supplies the major raw material Propylene and is stated to be able to meet the Company's full Propylene requirement, so there are no stated constraints on production capability
- Two alternative Propylene sources developed (BPCL and GAIL) for emergency need, though the Company states these are not economical due to high logistic costs
- Sales realisation supported by Anti-Dumping Duties imposed by the Govt. of India on imports of the product from certain countries
- Sustained safety record — 21.29 million accident-free man-hours over the last 17 years, National Safety Award 2025 (Prashansa Patra, 4th level) and FICCI Excellence in Safety 2025 award
- Associate of The Andhra Sugars Ltd., with The Andhra Sugars Limited and Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Limited as promoters

- Single-source raw-material dependence on Propylene from the HPCL refinery — MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' states the Company depends on its major raw material Propylene from a single source, the HPCL refinery. - Regulatory power-cost liabilities (FPPCA) under appeal — APERC, Kurnool levied Fuel & Power Purchase Cost Adjustment charges for FY2022-23 and FY2023-24, recovered in monthly instalments with regular power charges; the Company has appealed to APTEL, New Delhi, and the Board has made provisions pending disposal, which were recognised as exceptional items.
